key_insight: Replacing Cr with Cu in MnFeCoNi high-entropy alloys strengthens bifunctional alkaline water-splitting performance by tuning surface chemistry and intermediate binding.
engineering_relevance: Single-element substitution offers a practical design lever for cheaper, more efficient HEA electrocatalysts for alkaline HER and OER.
method: Compared CrMnFeCoNi (HEA-Cr) vs MnFeCoNiCu (HEA-Cu) under the same alkaline HER/OER conditions.
Combined electrochemical testing with computational electronic-structure and adsorption-energy analysis.
Examined post-OER surface reconstruction to assess element migration and catalyst stability.
evidence_signal: HEA-Cu showed lower overpotential and Tafel slope than HEA-Cr, with a reported overpotential of 538 mV and Tafel slope of 165 mV dec^-1.
watch_item: Cu migration during OER forms a Cu-rich outer shell, so long-term stability and reconstruction effects need careful validation.
paper_title: Structure-Property Correlation of Cr/Cu-MnFeCoNi High-Entropy Alloys for Alkaline Water Electrolysis
